subject: Renewal and retention: concession request for Atlas AI
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@atlasai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Atlas AI Finance <finance@atlasai.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation — pricing gap and next steps

Sofia / team,

Quick note from Atlas AI — our renewal for next quarter is under review and, after a recent budget reforecast, we have a significant gap vs. the current ARR. Our product team loves Redwood's latency and the integration has been rock-solid, but finance is pushing us to reduce vendor spend by ~25% across ML infra. At this point we are evaluating a smaller vendor footprint and part of that conversation will include not renewing at full rates unless we can land something meaningful on pricing or term structure.

Can we get a proposal with concrete concession options (discount, one-time credits, or term alignment) by next Wednesday? If not, we will likely move to a reduced footprint and staggered migration.

Thanks,
Claire Dunn\Head of Partnerships\Atlas AI

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@atlasai.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@atlasai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 12:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — pricing gap and next steps

Claire — thank you for the heads up and for the attached redlines. I understand the pressure from finance; we want to keep Atlas as a strategic customer.

High-level, I can offer a retention package that should bridge your immediate budget ask while keeping the integration and performance you rely on. The package I plan to propose to your team (pending internal approval) is:
- 25% off list for year 1 (applied as a one-time credit across invoices)
- A 30-day term reset (move renewal from calendar Q2 to Q3 to align budgets)
- Addendum for a 99.9% SLA overlay for the contract year with defined make-good credits (no change to core support tier)

I need a quick greenlight from our leadership for the discount + SLA addendum. Vivek / Marcus — can you review the ask below? I attached a cost impact worksheet I will send to finance.

If we can sign off on this package, I will send a DocuSign with the redline-friendly markup and an internal payment plan to your finance team.

Sofia Ivanova\Account Executive, Strategic Accounts\Redwood Inference\s: +1 415-555-0187

Attachments: cost_impact_q1-q4.xlsx (internal draft)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Feb 2028 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal conversation — concession ask from Atlas AI — approval required

Vivek / Marcus — forwarding Claire's note and Atlas' redline. TL;DR: customer asks for ~25% vendor spend reduction. Proposed retention package (what I need approval for):
- Concession: one-time 25% credit applied across first 12 months (impact = ~USD 120k ARR hit in year 1; see attached cost_impact_q1-q4.xlsx)
- Commercial: 30-day term reset to align with their revised budget cadence (no change to MRR / discount timing)
- Legal: SLA addendum guaranteeing 99.9% availability with make-good credits capped at 15% of monthly invoice in a quarter for verified incidents

Why approve: Atlas is a reference customer on latency-sensitive vision workloads; losing them would create churn risk and negative signals in the health vertical. Finance impact is concentrated to year 1 with return in year 2 assuming expansion expectations hold.

Request: please reply with APPROVE / APPROVE WITH MOD / DECLINE. If APPROVE, indicate whether the discount can be capped (e.g., 20% instead of 25%) or whether SLA language needs tighter legal review. I will coordinate DocuSign + finance payment terms.

Attachments: cost_impact_q1-q4.xlsx
